cause_quote: The new note wrapper split content with `const words = content.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);` and rejoined words with `const candidate = `${current} ${word}`;`, collapsing any run of spaces to one.
user_saw: In `openclaw configure`, a workspace path containing two consecutive spaces was shown with only one space in the summary note.
summary: The shared terminal note wrapper now keeps runs of ordinary spaces between words that fit on one line instead of rejoining words with a single space.
reasoning: The split-on-whitespace/rejoin-with-one-space logic was present verbatim in the commit that created the note wrapper (29884f8d, 'fix: wrap clack notes for cleaner boxes', read via gh api), and every later commit touching the file (perf, refactor, deslop) carried it forward unchanged. The wrapper never preserved repeated spaces, so the defect shipped with it; one could frame it as a regression of pre-wrapper clack note display, but the faulty code is the wrapper's original design.
